open.title: vLLM issue #36311 '[Feature Request] Pluggable KV cache eviction policy with attention sink protection'
open.who_is_asking: Community contributor (sahilmalik27 / sinkhole project) filing a feature request with a working monkey-patch proof of concept (sinkhole-vllm); asking vLLM maintainers to accept a BlockEvictionPolicy protocol upstream. The issue ends with four explicit open questions to maintainers, and states 'We are happy to submit this PR once the maintainers confirm the approach.'
open.verbatim_quote: vLLM's block manager evicts KV cache blocks with no awareness of **attention sink tokens** - a small set of tokens (typically 1-2) that absorb 45-55% of total attention mass across nearly all heads and layers. Evicting these tokens silently corrupts generation quality.
open.what_is_missing: No upstream sink-aware eviction exists in vLLM. The issue reports a reference implementation and a monkey-patch, not a merged feature. The requested components (BlockEvictionPolicy protocol, SinkAwareEvictionPolicy, EngineArgs.protect_sink_tokens, BlockSpaceManagerV2 guard) are all still proposed. The issue itself flags unowned paths: 'Are there chunked prefill or speculative decoding paths that also call free() and would need the guard?'

open.title: vLLM PR #43374 '[Core] Experimental session KV eviction with attention sinks'
open.who_is_asking: gtiwa (Meta, per the Signed-off-by) opening a 1,002-line PR; it is labelled needs-rebase and Open, and a competing implementer (nvbfalk) subsequently proposed converging on a different primitive.
open.verbatim_quote: After evicting positions [s, e), surviving tokens shift from position p to p - (e - s). Their cached K still carries the _old_ RoPE rotation. Without re-rotation, attention against post-eviction queries is numerically wrong on every RoPE model (LLaMA / Mistral / Qwen / Gemma / DeepSeek / Phi-3 / ...).
open.what_is_missing: The RoPE re-rotation kernel that would make this correct. Verbatim from the PR's 'Future work': 'In-tree RoPE re-rotation kernel + a default _post_add_requests implementation, after which the experimental env var can be removed. Copy-on-write path for the shared-block case (instead of raising).' The PR is gated behind VLLM_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_SESSION_EVICTION=1, raises RuntimeError when prefix caching shares blocks, requires an out-of-tree runner, and carries the needs-rebase label with merge conflicts as of 2026-06-03.

open.title: vLLM issue #47846 '[Feature]: model runner v2 support prefill context parallelism & cp8+tp8=worldsize8'
open.who_is_asking: yiminghub2024 (enterprise inference operator) comparing vLLM 0.24.0 against SGLang 0.5.14; confirmed and triaged by vLLM contributor hello-args and by yitingw1, a developer working on PCP/DCP.

open.title: vLLM RFC #51948 '[RFC]: Bounded-memory video sessions - KV retention for long-running streaming-input requests'
open.who_is_asking: nvbfalk (vLLM contributor) filing an RFC with a stated two-week feedback period, CC'ing njhill, ywang96, DarkLight1337, joshuadeng and others; a companion PR series #53871/#53876 is in Draft.
open.verbatim_quote: Sessions exist; memory management for sessions does not.
open.what_is_missing: A KV-manager primitive to free a block-aligned token range of a live request, scheduler-side retention/eviction/consolidation, and a session API. The RFC enumerates the gaps itself: '(1) a KV-manager primitive to free a block-aligned token range of a live request (today blocks are freed only when a request ends), with the freed blocks removed from the prefix-cache index so their content can never be served to anyone else; (2) scheduler-side retention/eviction/consolidation driven by per-session parameters...; (3) a thin frontend for the session lifecycle.' It also concedes a measurement gap: 'there is no public / open-source benchmark aiming at exactly this task and it's a known limitation.'

open.title: SGLang issue #27252 '[Roadmap] Prefill Context Parallel Refactor'
open.who_is_asking: SGLang collaborator Fridge003, filing the roadmap that the [CP V1 Deprecation N/5] series (#36222/#36223/#36228/#36229/#36230) implements. Still Open with 19 tasks.
open.verbatim_quote: The current context parallelism (CP) implementation has grown around model- and backend-specific branches. This makes the behavior hard to reason about and hard to extend.

DSA models support both zigzag and interleave; MLA and GQA models historically mostly supported zigzag; DeepSeek V4 uses interleave.' and 'Some topology choices are hardcoded in server args, such as forcing enable_dp_attention=True / dp_size=1 for interleave-style paths.' hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM blog: Efficient Decode Context Parallelism (DCP) benchmarks
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 8x NVIDIA B200 single node, serving Kimi K2.6 in NVFP4, concurrency 16-512. DCP is structurally multi-GPU: the documented GQA constraints require (tensor_parallel_size // num_key_value_heads) >= decode_context_parallel_size, so DCP needs at least 2 GPUs even in the best case.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim from the blog: 'We ran an experiment on a single 8xB200 node serving Kimi K2.6 in NVFP4 with vLLM'. Also: 'The DCP results in this post were measured on NVIDIA B200 GPUs with Kimi K2.6 in NVFP4'. The docs constraint is quoted from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/docs/serving/context_parallel_deployment.md.

hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM blog: GLM 5.3 Hybrid HiSparse Offloading benchmarks
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 8x H200 single node (TP8), GLM 5.3, 384 GiB host HiSparse pool + 128 GiB offload pool, max_num_batched_tokens=32768. Also requires a GLM 5.3-class sparse-MLA model plus a separate KV/tensor layout the target Qwen3-4B does not have.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim: 'We benchmarked GLM 5.3 on 8x H200 using an OpenHands multi-turn agentic workload' and 'Hybrid HiSparse enables running GLM 5.3 at full 1 million context length - previously impossible on this hardware'. The reproduction appendix uses --tensor-parallel-size 8. Additional scope limit: 'HiSparse is currently implemented only for NVIDIA GPUs.'

hw_ruled_out.title: SGLang HiCache official benchmark (LMSYS blog)
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: Two separate multi-GPU rigs: DeepSeek-R1 on 8x H20-3e using 3FS, and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 on 8x H800 GPUs with 8x mlx5 RDMA NICs using Mooncake. The 3FS path additionally needs a distributed filesystem; the Mooncake path needs RDMA and a metadata server cluster.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim from the benchmark section: '# DeepSeek R1 on 8 * H20-3e using 3FS' and '# Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 on 8 x H800 GPUs with 8 x mlx5 RDMA NICs using Mooncake', with launch commands using --tp 8.

hw_ruled_out.title: Moreh SLOPE: 'Optimizing Long-Context Prefill on Multiple (Older-Generation) GPU Nodes'
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 4-node AMD MI250 cluster, 8 devices per node (32 devices total), across-node context parallelism (Ulysses + Ring Attention). This is the clearest multi-node example: the entire premise is that 'prefill computation is confined to a single node' is the limitation being removed.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim: 'We evaluate SLOPE's prefill performance across different parallelization configurations combining Ulysses, Ring Attention, and Pipeline Parallel in various combinations, and compare it against SGLang with TP=8 on a 4-node AMD MI250 cluster (8 devices per node).' Note this source is a positive result for ring attention, not a negative one - it is listed here only because it cannot run on the target hardware.

hw_ruled_out.title: SGLang v0.5.19 release note: DCP on the trtllm_mla decode path
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: Eight B200s (Blackwell SM100) and the trtllm_mla / CuTe DSL / Tokenspeed MLA decode backends; the measured claim is specifically about an 8-GPU scaling curve. Not applicable to a single sm120 RTX PRO 6000 with a GQA model.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim from the release highlights: 'DCP on the default Blackwell MLA backend. Decode context parallelism now runs on trtllm_mla, not just CuTe DSL and Tokenspeed. It pays off at long context: at 128K input, plain TP stops scaling around 680 tokens per second on eight B200s, while DCP keeps going as concurrency grows ([#33926]).'

hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM RFC #34018 Helix benchmarks (and the SGLang mirror task #19436)
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 8x H200 single node (TP=8/DCP=4, DeepSeek-V2-Lite MLA) in the RFC body; GB200 NVL72 16-GPU for the follow-on numbers. Both are multi-GPU and the GB200 case additionally depends on NVL72-class NVLink connectivity; the RFC explicitly argues A2A 'provides lower latency when all GPUs have direct connectivity (NVSwitch)'.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim: 'E2E Results (H200 8-GPU, DeepSeek-V2-Lite MLA)' with a 256K/512K/1M TPOT table. A later comment in the same thread from the Zhipu Infra team enumerates further requirements: 'Cross-GPU KV Cache Storage (Interleaved Layout) - Support distributing KV cache across multiple GPUs...' and 'Due to GPU memory constraints during the prefill phase, a portion of the weights is asynchronously loaded via H2D transfer or gathered via all-gather to obtain the full weights.'

hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM issue #47846 - TP8 + PCP8 world-size explosion
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: The reporter is on one H20 8-GPU node and cannot start even CP8 alone. The error text documents the structural problem: 'Value error, World size (64) is larger than the number of available GPUs (8) in this node.' Contributor yitingw1 explains: 'vLLM TP8 PCP8==worldsize64, it uses cp8tp8 in attention... In vLLM, PCP is an independent dimension compared with TP. While in SGLang, CP is included in TP.'
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Full issue thread read via r.jina.ai, including the pasted server errors and both contributor replies.

hw_ruled_out.title: SGLang PR #38019/#38077 verification matrix - prefill CP correctness is only validated on multi-GPU H100/H200/B200 runners
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 4x H100 (the failing shard), 8-gpu-h200, 4-gpu-b200, 8-gpu-b300. There is no single-GPU prefill-CP configuration in play; the whole test matrix is multi-GPU.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim from the issue: 'on a 4x H100 node at current main.' and the CI labels quoted in PR #36228's verification table: H200: DeepSeek V3 CP + DSA prefill CP; B200: DeepSeek V4 FP4 CP + GPT-OSS MXFP4 CP; H100: GQA prefill CP; B300: GLM-5.2 PD/MTP/CP layer-split.

hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM x AgentX: agentic long-context serving at scale
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 12x GB300, 16x GB300, 2x B300, up to 1,000+ chips and ~2 MW; P/D disaggregation across nodes; DEP16/DCP8 configurations. Nothing in the reported results is reachable on one 96GB GPU.
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim from the results table and text: 'DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T | 12 GB300s / 256', 'Kimi K3 2.8T | 16 GB300s / 48', and 'run on a public benchmark infrastructure of more than 1,000 chips and roughly 2 MW of compute'.

hw_ruled_out.title: vLLM blog: Tiered KV Cache Offloading performance section
hw_ruled_out.hardware_requirement: 2x NVIDIA H100 (TP=2) for the headline capacity curve. The framework itself also needs a host DRAM tier sized well beyond the GPU KV cache ('For single-tier (CPU-only) setups, set cpu_bytes_to_use larger than the aggregate GPU KV cache').
hw_ruled_out.evidence: Verbatim benchmark setup: 'Model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 2x NVIDIA H100 (TP=2); Storage tier: filesystem backend on local NVMe; Workload: multi-turn conversations, 12K-token initial prompts + 4K tokens per round, 8 rounds; Max request concurrency: 64; Measures prefiller throughput only (prefill-decode disaggregated)'.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: vLLM AgentX blog, section 'The bitter lessons: where we failed and what we learned'
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_1_pipeline_parallelism: Pipeline parallelism (PP) does not fit warm agentic turns
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_1_body: Most agentic turns, however, already have system prompts and previous turns cached, and each new request may add only a few hundred or a few thousand tokens. There is not enough fresh computation to fill the pipeline efficiently, and pipeline bubbles consume much of the potential gain. The lesson is not that PP is ineffective. It is effective for cold, compute-heavy prefills, but it should not be the default for warm, prefix-heavy turns that dominate agentic sessions.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_2_dcp_on_dsv4: Decode context parallelism (DCP) does not transfer cleanly to DeepSeek V4
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_2_body: We invested heavily in overlapping communication with computation and in optimizing the corresponding kernels. Even after those improvements, DCP only matched DEP rather than surpassing it. The result reinforces a broader point from the execution-plane section: parallelism must follow model architecture. A strategy that succeeds for one latent-attention model may not generalize to another.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_3_multinode_dcp: At larger, multi-node DCP sizes, the communication cost of sharded attention outweighs the compute it saves.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_4_load_balance: Load balance does not guarantee better performance
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_4_body: However, in our experiments with AgentX, all of these policies underperformed simple session-aware sticky routing. The reason is cache locality... The system can therefore achieve a more balanced queue while processing fewer concurrent requests overall.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_5_chunked_prefill_hol: By default, vLLM's chunked-prefill scheduler runs in first-in, first-out order. One long prefill can claim the entire token budget step after step, and the short turns queued on the same rank cannot be scheduled at all until the long prefill finishes. This is known as head-of-line blocking
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_5_fix: With DeepSeek V4 Pro on B300s, this increases total tokens per GPU-second (TPGS) by up to 93% and improves P90 interactivity by roughly 2.3x. The trade-off is a higher TTFT for the long request itself, so TTFT-sensitive deployments should use a larger threshold.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote_6_pcp_limit: PCP shards the prompt sequence (the query tensor), distributing compressor and indexer work across ranks, while giving sparse MLA a wider, more efficient head-local shape. For a 32K prompt, PCP8 achieves a 2.65x prefill speedup over TP8, substantially reducing TTFT. However, it still replicates decode-side state across ranks, so it is best suited to dedicated prefill workers.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: vLLM CP docs: prefill context parallel is unfinished
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: Both approaches are under active development.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.context: Referring to the two prefill context parallel strategies (partial-query/full-KV, and partial-query/partial-KV using ring-attention). Contrast with the decode section, which is described as fully supported.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: TASP: Topology-aware Sequence Parallelism - ring attention communication inefficiency
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: However, it exhibits low communication efficiency, restricting its practical applicability. This inefficiency stems from the mismatch between the Ring AllGather communication primitive it adopts and the AlltoAll topology of modern accelerators. A Ring AllGather primitive is composed of iterations of ring-styled data transfer, which can only utilize a very limited fraction of an AlltoAll topology.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.what_it_reports: TASP reports 'up to 3.58 speedup than Ring Attention and its variant Zigzag-Ring Attention' on single-node and multi-node NVIDIA H100 systems and a single-node AMD MI300X system. Note the evaluation hardware is 8-GPU-class and the claimed wins are from replacing the ring primitive, not from ring attention being bad per se.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: Attention Entropy is a Key Factor: An Analysis of Parallel Context Encoding with Full-attention-based Pre-trained Language Models
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: Because parallel patterns are not encountered during training, naively applying parallel encoding leads to performance degradation. However, the underlying reasons and potential mitigations are unclear.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.what_it_reports: Identifies 'unusually high attention entropy' as the key factor, and finds that 'we adopt two straightforward methods to reduce attention entropy by incorporating attention sinks and selective mechanisms. Experiments on various tasks reveal that these methods effectively lower irregular attention entropy and narrow performance gaps.' This is a direct negative result for splitting a context into sub-pieces and encoding them in parallel: it degrades accuracy, and the paper's own mitigation is to add attention sinks. Venue: ACL 2025. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is about parallel context ENCODING (chunked/parallel prefill of one sequence), not about ring-attention transport, so it should not be over-generalised.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: KVDiagnosis: A Diagnostic Benchmark for KV-Cache Compression in Long-Context Language Models
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: First, a 25-method taxonomy groups methods into five mechanism families... On Qwen3-8B, four evidence-aware workloads yield 59 800 supported compressed runs over 2600 sources and 12 520 C-to-W rows. Under fixed diagnostic rules, 63.2% have low or partial measured/projected coverage. Only 19 rows (0.2%) combine high measured/projected coverage with strong likelihood drift
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.what_it_reports: A benchmark whose entire premise is that aggregate long-context task scores hide KV-compression failures: 'KV-cache compression reduces long-context memory, but aggregate task scores reveal neither which correct executions fail nor why.' It constructs FullCache-correct/compressed-wrong (C-to-W) sets per method and reports that 'all ten diagnostics separate failed from successful compression (stratified AUROC 0.684-0.871)'. Note this is a benchmark revealing failures, not a paper claiming compression is useless; it also reports a repair effect ('a controlled 4x evidence-attention boost repairs 29.2%').

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: The Spike, the Sparse and the Sink: Anatomy of Massive Activations and Attention Sinks (LeCun et al.)
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: Through systematic experiments, we show that the co-occurrence is largely an architectural artifact of modern Transformer design, and that the two phenomena serve related but distinct functions... We identify the pre-norm configuration as the key choice that enables the co-occurrence, and show that ablating it causes the two phenomena to decouple.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.what_it_reports: Attention sinks are an artifact of the pre-norm configuration and 'operate locally: they modulate attention outputs across heads and bias individual heads toward short-range dependencies' - i.e. they are not a general long-range retrieval mechanism. It does not claim sinks are useless; the vLLM feature request cites it as the formal characterisation of the phenomenon.

negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.title: MemGPT/Medha-adjacent head-of-line blocking claim for ring/striped attention
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.quote: Deploying million-token Large Language Models (LLMs) is challenging because production workloads are highly heterogeneous... This heterogeneity, combined with the quadratic complexity of attention, creates severe convoy effects where long-running requests stall short, interactive ones, degrading system responsiveness.
negative_result_findings_not_requiring_a.what_it_reports: The v5 abstract states: 'Medha makes preemption practical with a co-designed set of mechanisms -- including Adaptive Chunking and Stream Pipeline Parallel that overcome the perceived inefficiencies and scaling challenges of chunking.' IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the search snippet that surfaced this paper attributed a specific 'Ring and striped attention do not allow preemption of a long context prefill phase' claim to it, but the v5 ABSTRACT I actually retrieved does NOT contain that sentence, and the title in the snippet ('Mnemosyne: Parallelization Strategies...') does not match the retrieved title ('No Request Left Behind: Tackling Heterogeneity in Long-Context LLM Inference with Medha'). I am therefore recording only the abstract text I verified and flagging the chunking claim as NOT verified verbatim.
